analysis: Reviewed docs/architecture/inference.md head excerpts (lines 798-1209 and 1210-1628). The file is documentation only; the PR's visible patch (hunk ~2058-2077) changes Flint KV/checkpoint policy text: native KV and checkpoint precision are always used, provider-wide defaults are ignored, and Flint is paged-only with explicit paged treatment under automatic selection. The patch excerpt is truncated and that region is not in my supplied units, so I could not verify it directly. No executable code, authentication, attestation or encryption control changed in the supplied evidence. The assigned units mostly describe existing behavior: GLM native media and quarantine, tokenizer preflight, prompt-receipt calibration, deadlines, MTP drain and upgrade, sampling defaults, reasoning parsers, vision caps and paged dtype validation. The relevant prefix-cache threat T-041 is touched by statements that Flint uses paged KV plus a native checkpoint precision; these do not obviously alter the SSD cache HMAC naming, TTL, account scoping or KEK posture. I found no concrete regression or threat-model invalidation. Remaining integration questions: (1) the real Swift code for the Flint policy (EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve, EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend) is not supplied, so I cannot confirm that the docs match it and that failing closed on non-native or contiguous selection works; (2) whether Flint with paged KV and SSD prefix caching keeps the cache salt, scope and DBK3 bindings, which prefix-cache.md would document; (3) unchanged claims on GLM retained-fault memory charging, cache-salt scoping and the typical MTP acceptance default (approximate output) rely on code outside this batch.
